newsitem.title: INDIA: Nine policemen injured in India Kashmir blast.
newsitem.headline: Nine policemen injured in India Kashmir blast.

text.p: Nine policemen were injured on Sunday in India's troubled Jammu and Kashmir state when an explosive device tied to the body of a slain guerrilla went off, police said.

They said the explosion occurred when police were examining the body in Kupwara police station near the India-Pakistan border 87 km (55 miles) north of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state.
The explosive device was in a pouch tied to the body of a Moslem militant who was killed in a gunbattle on Saturday night in the same area, police said.
Over a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule in the Himalayan state where 20,000 people have been killed in a rebellion which erupted in 1990.
A car bomb explosion on Saturday evening in a crowded bus station in Jammu, the state's winter capital, killed 16 people and injured about 70.

The latest blast occurred on the third day of crucial talks between Indian and Pakistani diplomats in New Delhi. India and Pakistan have fought two wars over Kashmir since independence from Britain in 1947.
